headline: Scalable tools benchmark genome alignment, assembly, and phylogenetic inference methods
label: Scalable Genome Analysis Tools
summary: Recent preprints and a published OrthoFinder extension target runtime, memory, and accuracy limits in large-scale genome comparison.
synthesis: The common thread is methodological: each item addresses throughput, resource use, or evaluation fidelity in genome-scale analysis rather than reporting new biological findings. The seed-filter-extend study maps dependencies and dataflow across LASTZ, SegAlign, Darwin-WGA, and SNAP to locate serial bottlenecks. A fungal assembly benchmark over 66 simulated genomes and empirical reads reports that roughly 30-40X long-read coverage with 10-20X short-read polishing offers a balance. samsampleX provides distribution-aware downsampling for NGS benchmarking and outperforms uniform downsampling. DipSkmer estimates theta and pairwise distances from low-coverage diploid genome skims without a reference, using k-mers and coalescent theory. The RERconverge update reduces runtime, with core functions up to 28.6x faster. The OrthoFinder extension reports a 7% relative accuracy gain alongside reduced runtime and RAM. ECMME and PhyloZoo add selection-pressure resources and Python phylogenetic network tooling, respectively.
